questions.question: How do you build a counter with useReducer in React?
questions.title: Build a Counter with useReducer — React Example (TypeScript)
questions.direct_answer:
How do you build a counter with useReducer in React?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Action types (increment/decrement/reset/set), discriminated union, reducer function, useReducer hook, optional middleware.

**Classic weak answer:** Mutating state inside the reducer — reducers must return a new state object.

**Senior finish:** Add TypeScript discriminated union types, then extend the example to useContext for app-wide state.

interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Mutating state inside the reducer — reducers must return a new state object
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Add TypeScript discriminated union types, then extend the example to useContext for app-wide state

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **Build a Counter with useReducer — React Example (TypeScript)** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** How do you build a counter with useReducer in React?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **Action types (increment/decrement/reset/set), discriminated union, reducer function, useReducer hook, optional middleware**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Mutating state inside the reducer — reducers must return a new state object**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Add TypeScript discriminated union types, then extend the example to useContext for app-wide state**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** Action types (increment/decrement/reset/set), discriminated union, reducer function, useReducer hook, optional middleware
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

questions.question: How do you implement a useDebounce / useThrottle hook in React?
questions.title: useDebounce & useThrottle Hooks in React — Implementations
questions.direct_answer:
How do you implement a useDebounce / useThrottle hook in React?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** useEffect with setTimeout, cleanup on value change/unmount, stable callback via useRef, TypeScript generics.

**Classic weak answer:** Recreating the debounced function on every render — loses the timer reference; wrap in useRef or useMemo.

**Senior finish:** Compare useDebounce (debounce a value for search) vs useDebouncedCallback (debounce a function for event handlers).

interviewer_intent.testing: useEffect with setTimeout, cleanup on value change/unmount, stable callback via useRef, TypeScript generics
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Recreating the debounced function on every render — loses the timer reference; wrap in useRef or useMemo
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Compare useDebounce (debounce a value for search) vs useDebouncedCallback (debounce a function for event handlers)

questions.question: How do you implement infinite scroll in React?
questions.title: Infinite Scroll in React — Intersection Observer + React Query
questions.direct_answer:
How do you implement infinite scroll in React?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Intersection Observer ref for the sentinel row, paginated fetch (cursor or offset), React Query useInfiniteQuery, list virtualization for huge lists.

**Classic weak answer:** Using window scroll events for infinite scroll — rAF/throttle needed, janky; Intersection Observer is the modern approach.

**Senior finish:** Show useInfiniteQuery with Intersection Observer and react-virtual for performance; mention react-intersection-observer library.
